compared: after each case's steps: every session as Node's reader reads it from its log (valid, header, messages), whether every legacy json kept its bytes and mtime, and the leftover .tmp files; the disk-full case also after its failed run

excluded.a busy session is skipped and retried at: equality impossible: the core migrates at boot under the data dir's owner lock, before it serves anything, so no other writer can hold a session (Node migrates after boot, beside processes that may hold one); there is no busy state to skip
excluded.a file that fails verification is skippe: the case needs Node's test loader (`unstableLoad`: a document that loads differently on every read); the product's loader and the core read a json the same way every time, so no file fails this verification

loader: the product's LEGACY_SESSION_LOADER (the test passes its fixture loader); the claim is the test's held claim

product.tree: product tree loaded by the recorder
